Since the trains are traveling towards each other, we add their times together: 38.67 hours + 26 hours = 64.67 hours. Since a day has 24 hours, we divide by 24 to get the time they meet: 64.67 hours / 24 hours = 2.65 days. Since the trains leave at 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., respectively, we add their times together: 9:00 a.m. + 10:00 a.m. = 19:00 hours. Since the trains are traveling towards each other, we subtract their times together: 19:00 hours - 2.65 days = 16:35 hours. So the trains meet at 4:35 p.m. on the second day.

The two trains leave the same distance apart (195 miles), so they will meet after 195/60 = 3.25 hours or 3.25 hours * 60 minutes = 195 minutes. Since the trains are traveling towards each other, you need to subtract the time it takes for each train to travel to the meeting point from the total time. The first train takes 100 minutes to travel 195 miles (195/60), so it arrives at the meeting point at 9:20 a.m. The second train takes 100 minutes to travel 195 miles (195/80), so it arrives at the meeting point at 9:40 a.m. Since both trains arrive at the same time, the meeting happens at 9:20 a.m. + 100 minutes = 10:20 a.m.

The train from Austin leaves at 9:00 a.m. and travels 60 miles in 60 minutes (since speed is 60 mph). Since both trains travel on the same track, we can find the time when they meet by adding the time it takes for the Austin train to travel to the point where the two trains meet and subtracting the time it takes for the Dallas train to travel the same distance.

The Austin train takes 1 hour (60 minutes) to travel 60 miles, so it takes 60 minutes to travel 195 miles (385 minutes total). The Dallas train takes 1.5 hours (90 minutes) to travel 195 miles.
